solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ngaio Marsh, a rifle-toting heart-throb

indicators.note: to tote is to carry, so the words before it carry the solution inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first name, all of the surname, the article and most of the gun

explanation.surface: The detective novelist Ngaio Marsh pictured as a gun-carrying romantic idol.
explanation.walkthrough: Ngaio Marsh was a New Zealand crime writer, which makes the clue look like it wants an author or one of her characters; the punctuation and spaces are ignored inside the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian actor of Doctor Zhivago and Lawrence of Arabia was a famous screen idol adored by fans in the 1960s.

clue.text: Chap — Lawrence — put on gold cloak

blocks.note: a chap is a man
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A man named Lawrence dressing up in a golden cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence is reduced to the initials of the famous T. E. Lawrence; 'put on' simply strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteau is an old word, borrowed from French, for a loose outer cloak or mantle worn over clothes.

clue.text: Fast acceleration in inflation measure (Germany)

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a is the physics symbol for acceleration
the Retail Prices Index, a UK measure of inflation
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An economic report on a sudden jump in German inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: The RPI (Retail Prices Index) is a British inflation figure; the bracketed Germany sits at the end as its car-sticker letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and fast are plain synonyms, both describing movement or change happening at high speed.

clue.text: CIA head arranged to acquire new house down south

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so a letter is added among the others
letters that are arranged are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The head of the CIA buying a new property in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the CIA's boss but is simply four letters of the mix; 'down south' points to Latin America rather than the US South.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or main dwelling in Spain and Spanish-speaking Latin America, far to the south of the US.

clue.text: Dad’s carnations went mad after being fed by gallon bucket

indicators.note: being fed means having something put inside, so one letter goes into the rest
going mad means losing all order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
G is the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: Father's carnations ran riot after being given a whole gallon bucket of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' looks like the container for the gallon, but it is the verb, as in 'it's bucketing down', and it stands at the end as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bucket, in British informal use, is to pour with heavy rain, the same as the idiom for a downpour.

clue.text: “Not applicable” entered in dossier in the end

indicators.note: something that has entered a place is now inside it

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of papers
N/A is the form-filling abbreviation for not applicable

explanation.surface: Someone finally wrote 'not applicable' in an official dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads like an adverb for 'finally', but 'in' is the link and 'the end' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, so the concluding section or end.

clue.text: Georgina, exhausted, starts to produce enormous yawn

indicators.note: an exhausted thing is emptied out, so only the outer shell of the word is left
starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the name with its insides taken away
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A tired Georgina gives a huge yawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' looks like a description of a sleepy Georgina, but it tells you to empty her name, leaving its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, and a yawn is such a wide opening, used here as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Terrorist chap pretends to cuddle wife

indicators.note: cuddling means wrapping your arms round someone, so one part encloses another

blocks.note: a chap is a guy
to pretend is to fake
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A violent man feigns affection by hugging his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes was one of the Gunpowder Plotters who tried to blow up the English Parliament in 1605, still remembered every 5 November on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: He plotted to kill the king with explosives under Parliament, an act of political violence that fits the modern word for it.

clue.text: Suggest something struck by model?

blocks.note: first meaning: put forward an idea
second meaning, read in two parts: a professional's posture, the kind a fashion model strikes

explanation.surface: Hinting at what a model might be hit by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck' suggests a blow, but models strike poses; the question mark flags that the second meaning splits the word into PRO and POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward a plan or idea for consideration, which is exactly what suggesting means.

clue.text: Cut nails back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run from the end

blocks.note: pins are small nails

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim your fingernails short.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'nails' fingernails and 'cut back' a phrase; here nails are the metal fasteners.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors, and to snip is to cut with quick short strokes.

clue.text: Python and mice on the loose in part of the house

indicators.note: animals on the loose run about freely, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake and some mice have escaped somewhere in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' just joins the two words of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney pot is the clay pipe fitted on top of a chimney stack, one component of a building's roof.

clue.text: Latam country impounds diamonds European concealed

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something up inside a pound or enclosure

blocks.note: Peru is a Latin American country; Latam is short for Latin America
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A South American state seizes smuggled European diamonds that had been hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Peru encloses the diamonds letter and the European letter follows on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdue, from French for lost, describes something hidden away out of sight, as in lying in ambush unseen.

clue.text: In Spain, bubbly parties filled with Liberal spirit

indicators.note: a thing filled with something has that something inside it

blocks.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a do is a party, so dos are parties

explanation.surface: Spanish celebrations full of fizz and generous drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' tempts you towards political parties beside 'Liberal', but here it means social dos.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy distilled in Normandy, a strong alcoholic drink of the kind called spirits.

clue.text: Wine beginning to mesmerise American trainee officer

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter
US for the United States, so American
a cadet is an officer in training

explanation.surface: A glass of wine starts to charm a young American recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the very start, so 'beginning' belongs to the wordplay, not to 'Wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white produced in the Loire valley of France, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Drink tea, name “PG Tips”

indicators.note: tipping things over spills them out, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert line telling you to drink tea and name PG Tips, a British teabag brand.
explanation.walkthrough: PG Tips is a famous British tea brand, so the whole surface is about tea; but 'Tips' is the anagram signal and only PG belongs in the mix with NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine, a beverage, so it is an example of something you drink.

clue.text: Moose knocked over European painter

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: in Europe the moose is called an elk
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A moose bowls over a European artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' reads as describing the painter but supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German artist of the twentieth century, famous for colourful abstract canvases.

clue.text: Claim husband vanished from Yorkshire spa town

indicators.note: what has vanished from a place is no longer there, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a husband disappeared from Harrogate.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is an English spa town in Yorkshire; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or take something for yourself without any right, as when laying claim to power.

clue.text: Madame reviewed author’s first novel

indicators.note: to re-view is to look back over, so the letters are read backwards
first means the opening position, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: Mme is the abbreviation for Madame
initial letter

explanation.surface: A French lady critiques a writer's debut book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' suggests a book critic, but it reverses the abbreviation; 'author's first' is not the author's debut novel but the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a matchmaking young woman, a classic example of English fiction.

clue.text: Country doctor left last of boiled eggs

indicators.note: the last of anything is its final part, so only the end letter is kept

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
L is the abbreviation for left
final letter
ova are egg cells

explanation.surface: A rural GP walked out leaving the last of the boiled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' looks like a single phrase about a rural GP, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a small landlocked nation in Eastern Europe, between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: Adult underwear is the wrong way round; leg sore

indicators.note: the wrong way round means facing the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
a bra is an item of underwear
taken as written
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Someone has put their underwear on back to front and has a sore leg from the chafing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wrong way round' seems to describe the underwear but affects only the two-letter word after it; 'leg' is the cricket term, where leg side and on side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a graze where skin has been scraped away, a sore patch on the body.

clue.text: Best man, gemstone rings

indicators.note: to ring something is to circle it, so one part surrounds another

blocks.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A best man buying the wedding rings set with gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' looks like the wedding role and 'rings' like wedding bands; split them, so 'Best' is the definition and 'rings' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the most favourable or effective possible, which is another way of saying top or finest.

clue.text: Associate with The Devil, Jack?

blocks.note: Hob is an old name for a goblin or the Devil
in cribbage, his nob is the jack of the turned-up suit

explanation.surface: A question whether Jack is in league with Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is the playing card, which in the card game cribbage is called 'his nob'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially and chat, especially with people of higher status, so to keep company.

clue.text: Doris lap dancing where truckers leave the M1?

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doris giving a lap dance at a motorway truck stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; a slip road is the ramp for joining or leaving it, and the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries leaving a British motorway take the short exit ramp linking it to other roads, hence the question-marked example definition.

clue.text: Decorated knight dressed in gold had dinner

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
N is the chess notation for knight
to have dinner is to eat, so had dinner is ate

explanation.surface: A decorated knight in golden armour sat down to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated knight' reads as one phrase, a knight with medals; 'Decorated' alone is the definition, and the knight in gold is gold followed by knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately adorned with ornament, the adjective for something heavily embellished.

clue.text: Arrest former pupil, one with great wealth

blocks.note: to nab is to arrest
OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: Police detain a wealthy former student.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy (OB) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a European who made a fortune in India, and now any very rich, powerful person.

clue.text: Unpleasant woman sent back a 50 ounce cheese

indicators.note: what is sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a gorgon is a fierce, ugly woman, after the Medusa myth
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for 50
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A rude customer returns a fifty-ounce chunk of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' looks like returning a dish but reverses only the three pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese made from cow's milk, a specific dairy product.

clue.text: Strike bottom softly

blocks.note: bum is British slang for the bottom
p (piano) is the musical marking for softly

explanation.surface: A gentle smack on someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum is everyday British slang for the buttocks; p stands for piano in music.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump is to knock or hit against something, so it is a synonym for a light blow.

clue.text: Healthy precipitation reported

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: hail is frozen precipitation

explanation.surface: A weather forecast saying the rainfall is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: Precipitation could be rain, snow or sleet; only the icy kind fits the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale means strong and in good condition, usually of an older person, as in 'hale and hearty'.

clue.text: Court action ruined kebab stall

indicators.note: a ruined thing is broken apart, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawsuit has put a kebab vendor out of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' looks like legal proceedings; it is the sport played on a court.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is played on an indoor court, so the activity happening there is the sport itself.
